questions.question: Who made the obelisk, and what does its inscription say?
What future quest and reward involve the obelisk?

description:
Below the South Coast Road, fishermen share a substantial pond with hooks, nets, bait-stealing Aipom and an Oran tree. The visible Psyduck stands at the western shallow bank. Its encounter is voluntary: approaching it offers a battle at level 8, and capture or defeat removes that individual. Toma says they leave this bank to the duck when the road gets noisy. Pond grass has a stronger local mix of Psyduck, Sunkern and Aipom than the road grass farther north.

A narrow concealed trail turns west through the thicket, then follows the pond’s western side south to a visible old basket. Dry leaves cover a waxed-cloth bundle containing Mystic Water; collecting it leaves the hollow empty. The trail is reachable on foot and the repaired tree edges keep its way through readable. Farther around the bank, a different fishing basket is patched with three kinds of twine and has a tiny fish carved into its handle. These are distinct objects.

The island obelisk remains separated by water and requires Surf to reach; Surf is not awarded here. Its marks are worn too shallow to read. Origin, purpose and future reward remain open.

Proposed bank routine: bait is kept in lidded boxes weighted with stones after repeated Aipom thefts. A clean landing beside the tree is kept clear of discarded hooks; the muddier feeding edge belongs to the creatures until somebody needs to land a boat. Help can mean collecting abandoned line or moving a dropped bait box, with the resulting clear patch still visible on a later visit. Optional battles are invitations away from the line-tending work, not the price of using the bank. None of this explains the obelisk or makes an ordinary fish catch into a relic.

sections: §32: pond, fishermen, relocated Psyduck and unresolved obelisk.

data.description: Road layout, named pond entrances and the declared western trail establish the accessible bank, reward basket and isolated obelisk.

name: The pond below the South Coast Road
